transcript:
customer_acme_ml: Hey team, hitting 413s and occasional dimension-mismatch errors when streaming a huge embeddings batch (approx 120k vectors) to /v1/embeddings. We stream chunks ~2MB each using Transfer-Encoding: chunked. Some requests 413, some succeed but results later fail with "dimension mismatch: expected 768 got 0" during post-processing. Any ideas?

olivia_support: Sorry you're seeing this — can you paste the raw curl you use and the exact error payloads? Also which model/dim are you targeting (e.g., text-embedding-3-small => 1536)?

customer_acme_ml: Repro snippet:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @batch_stream.json \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
```
batch_stream.json is a concatenation of many JSON objects separated by newlines (we stream an NDJSON-like body). Response for failing request:
```
HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
{"error":"request body too large"}
```
When it succeeds server returns 200 but downstream job in our pipeline raises:
```
ValueError: dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 0
```

raj_engineer: Thanks for details. Two separate things here likely: 413 from proxy or load balancer (client_max_body_size / request size limits), and the dimension=0 indicates something went wrong in reassembly or our streaming parser dropped payload for one message. Do you have per-chunk boundaries always aligned to JSON objects? If you split inside a base64 or string, our reassembler expects newline-delimited records.

customer_acme_ml: We do newline-delimited JSON objects, but each object may span multiple chunks. We assumed streaming reassembly handles that.

raj_engineer: It should — but there was a recent edge-case where a chunk boundary splitting a multi-byte unicode escape or base64 could cause the parser to return an empty embedding vector for that record. We're tracking an issue (ENG-embeds-4521). Workaround: ensure each chunk ends with a full record boundary (i.e., flush per-record) or use smaller per-record sizes (~512KB). Also try sending Content-Length when you can (disable Transfer-Encoding chunked) — some proxies treat chunked bodies differently.

cody_infra: Also check upstream NGINX / Envoy limits. 413 is classic client_max_body_size in nginx. On our side LB has default 1MB for some older routes. If you hit the hosted API, we have automatic routing but older edge nodes had smaller thresholds. I'll check route telemetry.

lina_sre: Additional config to watch: proxy_request_buffering (nginx) — if enabled, it buffers entire request to disk and can return 413 early; also client_body_buffer_size, client_max_body_size, and proxy_buffers. For Envoy, check max_request_bytes and stream idle/timeouts.

customer_acme_ml: Is there a recommended chunk size we should aim for to avoid both 413s and parser bugs?

olivia_support: Recommended pragmatic settings:
- Chunk target: 256KB–1MB per chunk for NDJSON streaming.
- If you can, send one record per chunk for safest reassembly.
- For very large batches (>50k vectors), use presigned S3 multipart upload + reference-only payloads (upload vectors to S3, then call embeddings with pointers) — that avoids HTTP request limits entirely.
- If you must stream, try gzipping the payload and set Content-Encoding: gzip — smaller body less likely to hit proxy limits. We support gzip for embeddings ingestion.

raj_engineer: For reproducible steps we use locally:
1) Create 5k newline JSON objects with 1536-dim floats. (script attached below)
2) Stream via python requests generator with chunk_size=512*1024.
3) Observe responses & tail server logs with `tail -f /var/log/redwood/ingest.log` to see parser warnings.

Example python generator (workable repro):
```
def gen(records):
    for r in records:
        yield (json.dumps(r) + "\n").encode('utf-8')

requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=gen(records))
```

cody_infra: If you can share the failing gzipped chunk (or hash of it) we can grep logs and correlate. We saw repeated 413s on edge-node-7 over the last 12 hours — increasing client_max_body_size to 16M on that node reduced 413s for some customers.

customer_acme_ml: I can reproduce with a smaller set. Trying the python generator with chunk_size 256K now. Also switching to one-record-per-chunk easy for our pipeline.

olivia_support: Great—while you test, we'll open a support investigation. Actions from our side:
- cody will check LB/nginx route thresholds and bump when safe (Cody: pls note nodes with the old config).
- raj will link ENG-embeds-4521 to this thread and prioritize the parser hardening fix (avoid dimension=0 outputs).
- Support will recommend presigned S3 flow as long-term for >100k vectors.

ci-bot: Ticket created: SUP-7891; linked ENG-embeds-4521; infra alert created: INFRA-3132.

customer_acme_ml: After forcing one-record-per-chunk the 413s stopped and no dim=0 errors so far. Thanks. We'll keep testing and share logs if anything else appears.

olivia_support: Perfect. If you hit the 413 again, please include the full curl -v output and the `Via`/`X-Request-Id` response headers so we can trace the exact edge node. Marking this thread for escalation tracking.

raj_engineer: Quick note for others: short-term mitigation we applied to some edge pools is raising client_max_body_size to 16M and disabling request buffering for streaming routes. Long-term fix: parser/state machine fix to correctly reassemble across chunk boundaries even with multibyte splits.

customer_acme_ml: Appreciate the rapid help! We'll switch to S3 pointers for the big nightly batch and use per-record-chunking for near-real-time ingest.

olivia_support: Thanks — closing loop when ENG confirms patch. :thumbsup:
